resolution: fixed (27.5) — the arrow detector now claims the bare Arrow IPC *stream* framing (a continuation-marked `Schema` message first, then well-formed `RecordBatch`/`DictionaryBatch` messages, ending in an end-of-stream marker) in addition to the file format (magic+footer) and the historical magic+padding-prefixed stream; all four `arrow-stream-*.stream` samples are now claimed as `arrow`. The legacy pre-0.15 no-continuation framing is deliberately declined (a magic-less source has no other anchor, and the stream parser admits only the continuation form). Regression tests `arrow_adapter::stream_framing_is_detected_and_messages_are_ordered_and_exact`, `arrow_adapter::stream_near_misses_decline_to_opaque`, and court `tools/phase27-5-1-arrow-stream-court.sh` (src/adapter/arrow.rs).

recorded misclassification (precedence) — the reST detector is tried before AsciiDoc and claims `asciidoctor-CHANGELOG.adoc`, `asciidoctor-locale-attributes-ja.adoc`, `asciidoctor-locale-attributes-sr.adoc`, `asciidoctor-pages-macos.adoc`, and `asciidoctor-pages-stylesheet-modes.adoc` via its field-list (`:name: value`) signal; AsciiDoc attribute entries are syntactically RST field lists, and reordering AsciiDoc before reST is not clearly warranted (reST precedence is load-bearing), so it is not reordered. Phase 28.1 re-checked each and left them recorded rather than contaminating reST (src/adapter/rst.rs, asciidoc.rs).

fixed (28.1) — `asciidoctor-cli-nav.adoc` is now claimed as AsciiDoc. It is a navigation page that is *only* a list of AsciiDoc cross-reference macro calls (`* xref:index.adoc[]`, nested `** xref:man1/asciidoctor.adoc#options[CLI Options]`), which reST and Markdown cannot produce (`xref:target[…]` is an AsciiDoc-only call). A new narrow byte-level signal (`is_xref_macro_list`: ≥2 non-blank lines, every line a list item whose whole text is an `xref:<target>[…]` call) admits it; a plain bullet list without `xref:` macros still stays Opaque. Regression test `asciidoc::tests::detects_a_cross_reference_list_and_declines_its_negations` (src/adapter/asciidoc.rs).

recorded (unchanged reason) — two of the three recorded CBOR declines are genuine detector boundaries and stay recorded: `cbor-data-integer.cbor` is a lone scalar (`18 2a`, 2 bytes) below the deliberate structural bar; `cbor-rfc8949-good.cbor` is a genuinely well-formed single map whose deepest RFC 8949 vector nests to **512 levels**, above the deliberate `max_cbor_depth` cap of 256, so it is declined on the DoS bound (raising that cap to admit one sample is not warranted). The third, `cbor-data-tagged_date.cbor`, is fixed — see the `cbor`/`cbor` note below. The lone-scalar and depth declines are conservative by design (src/adapter/cbor.rs).

fixed (28.1) — `cbor-data-tagged_date.cbor` (tag 0 around a text date string, 22 bytes) is now claimed as CBOR. A **top-level tag** (major type 6) is itself a strong, self-identifying CBOR construct, so the detector now admits a root tag at `MIN_TAG_DETECT_NODES` (2: the tag plus its one tagged item) rather than requiring the container floor of `MIN_DETECT_NODES` (3); the same bytes without the tag lead are a bare text string (a scalar) and still decline. Regression test `cbor::tests::detects_a_tagged_scalar_and_rejects_a_bare_scalar` (src/adapter/cbor.rs).

recorded decline — `poi-document-Bug60942b.doc` stays here: it is a **Word 6.0** FIB (`wIdent` 0xA5DC, `nFib` 0x0065), outside the supported Word 97-2003 `nFib` subset the adapter models, so it stays at the generic CFBF layer. The second recorded cause, `poi-document-testRangeDelete.doc` (a genuine Word FIB whose `WordDocument` mini-stream is **fragmented** and whose **root mini stream is itself fragmented**), is **fixed (28.1)**: a mini sector's absolute position is now resolved through the root mini stream's FAT chain (`CfbfModel::mini_chain`, added in model version 2), so `cfbf::stream_leading`'s first-chunk prefix read works for a fragmented mini stream; regression test `legacy_cfbf_detection::fragmented_mini_stream_in_fragmented_root_stream_is_detected` (src/adapter/cfbf.rs, doc.rs).

recorded decline — the sample is an **mbox** (a leading `From ` envelope line, not an RFC 5322 header) whose `multipart/report` boundary is folded and truncated (`;\n\tbo`), so the bounded header-block scan declines rather than admitting an unmodellable message container (src/adapter/eml.rs).

fixed — GPX 1.0 (`http://www.topografix.com/GPX/1/0`, same `gpx` dialect) and a **namespace-less** `<kml>` with a recognized structural child are now claimed (src/adapter/gis.rs, `declares_ns` + `GPX_1_0_NS`); regression tests `gis::tests::detects_kml_and_gpx_and_rejects_junk` and `gis_adapter::detection_is_byte_based_and_conservative`.

recorded misclassification (precedence) — `loghub-Windows-Windows_2k.log` is still claimed by the CSV detector (consistent field count) before the (later) logstream detector runs; reordering risks the load-bearing CSV detector, so it is not reordered (src/adapter/logstream.rs, csv.rs).

recorded decline + fixed (28.1) — `loghub-HPC-HPC_2k.log` stays recorded: it is a space-separated event record with **no timestamp and no level** (`134681 node-246 unix.hw state_change.unavailable …`), which is not a log-stream line grammar and is left to the fixed-width/tabular heuristics. Three other declines are **fixed**: the detector's generic grammar now also accepts a `YY/MM/DD HH:MM:SS` slash timestamp (Spark) and a bracketed `[MM.DD HH:MM:SS]` timestamp (Proxifier), and a new BSD-without-`<PRI>` dialect accepts `Mmm dd hh:mm:ss host tag…: msg` (macOS `loghub-Mac-Mac_2k.log`, whose lenient tag region can embed spaces and `([pid])`). Detection stays conservative (≥2 non-blank lines, **every** non-blank line must match). Regression tests `logstream::tests::detects_the_widened_dialects` and `logstream::tests::the_widened_grammar_still_declines_prose` (src/adapter/logstream.rs).
